content: Start by reading TASK.md, then complete the assignment.

content.content:
1	# Task 2: forest of 10,000 instances
2	
3	Build a scene with Aura3D (`@aura3d/engine`, already installed in node_modules).
4	
5	Requirements:
6	1. A ground plane and exactly 10,000 scattered objects drawn with instancing (not 10,000 separate meshes): 8,000 trees (a trunk and a canopy, each instanced) and 2,000 rocks.
7	2. Placement is deterministic from a fixed seed (same forest every load), no overlaps needed.
8	3. Per-instance colour variation (canopies and rocks do not all share one colour).
9	4. One directional light that casts shadows, and exponential fog.
10	5. The camera slowly orbits the forest and the whole scene is visible.
11	
12	The rendering contract in the next section applies.
13	
14	## Rendering contract (all tasks)
15	
16	- Draw into the existing `<canvas id="app">` (640x360 CSS pixels, device pixel ratio 1). Do not resize it or create another canvas.
17	- Render continuously with `requestAnimationFrame`. When the first frame has been drawn set `window.__EVAL_READY__ = true`.
18	- No network access: load assets only from `/assets/...` (served from `public/assets`). Do not import from CDNs.
19	- Code goes in `src/` (TypeScript, strict). The entry is `src/main.ts`. It must pass `typecheck` and build with `vite build`.
20	- When you are done, call `finish`.
21

content.thinking: I'm setting up the main scene logic—timing the ready state after an animation frame, configuring camera orbit with auto-rotate, and tuning scene scale, fog density, and shadow coverage for the right visual balance.

input.summary: I wrote src/main.ts. It builds a 260×260 ground plane and 10,000 instanced objects in three instanced nodes: 8,000 trunks, 8,000 canopies and 2,000 rocks. Positions come from a fixed-seed LCG (seed 12345). Canopies and rocks get per-instance HSL colours on a white base material. The scene has one shadow-casting directional light, a hemisphere fill light, and exponential fog (`effects.fog`, density 0.0045). The camera is `camera.orbit` with `autoRotate`, placed at [0, 85, 130] to keep the whole forest in view. `window.__EVAL_READY__` is set after `app.ready()` and two animation frames. `typecheck` passes. I did not run `vite build` or render the scene, so the look, shadow coverage and fog strength are unchecked. Also, `__EVAL_READY__` is set after two `requestAnimationFrame` ticks rather than inside the engine's own render loop, so it doesn't strictly confirm the first frame was drawn.
